correctness.rationale: Exact constant-acceleration integration gives F_r(t)=[[1-rt²/2,t-t²/2],[-rt,1-t]], determinant 1-t+rt²/2 and trace 2-t-rt²/2. Jury gives single-step interval (0,min(2,2/r)). For product the first two tests hold automatically, while 2(1+T+D)=8-4(a+b)+4(1-r)ab+r²a²b². Holding ab fixed and using a+b<L+ab/L reduces the infimum to one boundary edge; direct quadratic minimization yields all four cases, including strictly interior stability at zero boundary infima. Independent symbolic algebra and 896 rational pairs corroborated; true proof is real-variable optimization.

value.rationale: Two individually Schur-stable held-feedback maps can destabilize each other: sharp universal safe-gain intervals and rational witness quantify a genuine noncommutative stability obstruction. Exact gain phase boundaries and infimum Jury margin are natural control invariants, not parameter relabelling or an arbitrary tiny-instance enumeration.

limitations: Ideal scalar double integrator with full-state fixed PD feedback and two alternating positive held steps. No arbitrary-switching guarantee, stochastic jitter, nonlinear dynamics, or uniform transient bound.
